primitives.name: Functional Spline Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: (1) Functional component f_i(t) = Σ_{m=1}^{80} θ_im b_m(t): cubic B-splines (80 df; 120 df in model M4) with a sparse latent-factor model on coefficients θ_im = Σ_l λ_ml η_il + ξ_im, λ under a Bhattacharya–Dunson multiplicative-gamma-process shrinkage prior (adaptive number of factors k ≪ p).

primitives.name: GARCH Seasonal Intercept Model

primitives.assumptions: Inter-seasonal jumps follow a GARCH process; volatility clusters over time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When α_1 + π ≥ 1, leading to non-stationary volatility.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that athletic performance evolves both smoothly over time (via functional splines) and in discrete jumps between seasons (modeled via GARCH errors on intercepts). This dual structure allows for accurate modeling of aging, form fluctuations, and volatility clustering. The functional spline approach enables capturing complex intra-seasonal trends while the GARCH component addresses inter-seasonal variance. The latent factor model introduces parsimony by reducing dimensionality of athlete-specific coefficients. These primitives together support a unified framework where performance is decomposed into smooth, stochastic, and structured components. Failure modes include overfitting due to too many splines, non-stationarity in GARCH, or insufficient shrinkage in latent factors. The mathematical duality lies in separating temporal smoothness from volatility dynamics, which mirrors how GSI treats variance and trend separately in its Bayesian inference pipeline.
